Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has spoken warmly about Barcelona star Lamine Yamal after the teenage forward showed kindness to Rice’s young son following a recent match between the two clubs. Rice revealed that his son is a huge admirer of Yamal and was initially unsettled by the prospect of his father lining up against the player he idolises. As reported by Fabrizio Romano on X on Sunday, Rice was quoted as saying, “My son is a huge fan of Lamine. I told him I was going to play against him, and he kept asking me why I was going to face Lamine.” After the game, Yamal took time to interact with the boy in a gesture that clearly left an impression on the England international. “But Lamine was really lovely to him, and as a father, I really appreciated that gesture. Such kindness,” Rice continued. EPL: Rice confirms new Arsenal contract is close Spain not racist, says coach De la Fuente ahead of England clash ‘Truly beautiful’ to make football return, says Ronaldinho The Arsenal player suggested Yamal’s caring nature may stem from his own family responsibilities. “I know he has a younger brother he looks after, so I think it comes naturally to him. I was really touched by that gesture. It shows just how respectful and humble Lamine is.” The comments highlight a lighter, more human side to the intense rivalry between two of Europe’s top clubs and underline the respect Yamal, still only a teenager, commands both on and off the pitch.
